text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No generative AI or personal data review recorded","detail":"The proposal deploys a GenAI/LLM chatbot that identifies customers by phone number and accesses order history (personal data). No AI governance, privacy, or security review is recorded; only vendor selection status is mentioned.","evidence_quote":"Deploy a GenAI chatbot using an LLM that identifies the customer by phone number and answers order status questions from order history.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record completed generative AI review and privacy/data protection review (including phone-number identification and vendor data handling) before launch."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Unsourced 60% deflection claim","detail":"The 60% contact deflection expectation is stated as a quantitative claim with no source, benchmark, or pilot data.","evidence_quote":"We expect the chatbot to deflect 60% of contacts.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite a source (vendor benchmark, pilot, historical analysis) or reframe as a hypothesis with a justified range."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Vague success metric 'Customer happiness'","detail":"'Customer happiness' is not a canonical glossary metric (e.g., CSAT, Contact Rate); it is ambiguous about the survey, scale, and population.","evidence_quote":"Customer happiness: from 4.0 to 4.4 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Replace with a canonical defined metric (e.g., Contact CSAT or Delivery CSAT) and specify how it is measured."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for chatbot accuracy and escalation","detail":"The chatbot changes the support contact experience, yet guardrails such as escalation/handoff to human, repeat contact rate, and answer accuracy/hallucination rate are absent. Deflection could hide unresolved issues.","evidence_quote":"- Contact Rate: stop if it rises by more than 1 per 100.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as repeat contact rate, human escalation rate, wrong-answer/hallucination rate, and resolution rate."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of standard and misaligned with metric window","detail":"A 3-week duration meets the 14-day minimum, but the 12-week success metric timeframe is not covered by it. Also the MDE of 0.5 contacts per 100 applies to contact rate, not the stated primary success metric (happiness 4.0→4.4), so power is not established for the primary metric.","evidence_quote":"Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.5 contacts per 100, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align duration, MDE, and power with the primary success metric and its 12-week horizon, or revise the timeframe."}]}
